request.spec:
Show on each person the due of their OPEN and PENDING claims that count, split by the age of
the claim on the sheet's today (the days from the claim's date): aged 0 to 30 days, 31 to 60, and
61 or more. A claim dated after today counts as 0 to 30.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person the due of their OPEN and PENDING claims that count, split by the age of
the claim on the sheet's today (the days from the claim's date): aged 0 to 30 days, 31 to 60, and
61 or more. A claim dated after today counts as 0 to 30.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now shows how much is due on their OPEN and PENDING claims, split by how old each claim is on the sheet's today: 0–30 days, 31–60 days and 61 days or more. All 4 tests in the spec pass under `bin/e2e`.

The change is all in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. I didn't need to touch the server or the stored data, because this screen already works out every per-person figure, including the due total, in the browser.

- **New columns:** three cells in each person's row, tagged `person-aged-0-30`, `person-aged-31-60` and `person-aged-61`.
- **What counts:** the same claims the person's live totals use. Claims on hold, deferred or past the person's retirement date are left out, and so are claims with no due (shown as n/a). Each claim's due is the figure the claims table shows, late charge and floor included.
- **Age:** the number of days from the claim's date to the sheet's today. A claim dated after today goes in 0–30. If the sheet has no today set, all three columns show 0.00.
- **Cap:** the three columns are not reduced to the sheet's cap the way the due total is, so when a person is over the cap the three won't add up to their due total.

Nothing new is written to the audit file, since the spec doesn't expect any new records.
